item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 241755
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
Issued by the NWS Weather Prediction Center College Park MD
1100 AM PDT Thu Sep 24 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, located about 100 miles offshore of southwestern Mexico, on
Hurricane Odalys, located well west-southwest of the southern tip
of Baja California, and on Tropical Storm Nolo, located a few
hundred miles south of the Big Island of Hawaii.

South of the Gulf of Tehuantepec:
An area of low pressure is expected to form in a couple of days to
the south of the Gulf of Tehuantepec. Afterwards, environmental
conditions should be favorable for gradual development, and a
tropical depression is likely to form early next week as the system
moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward, parallel to the
coast of southern and southwestern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
An area of low pressure could form about 1000 miles east-southeast
of the Hawaiian Islands over the weekend. Environmental conditions
could support some gradual development of this system, and a
tropical depression could form during the early middle portion of
next week. The system is forecast to move generally northeastward,
remaining well east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

$$
Forecaster Pierce/Brown

--------------------

DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM PDT (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Odalys was located
near latitude 16.8 North, longitude 124.9 West. Odalys is moving
toward the east-northeast near 8 mph (13 km/h), and this general
motion should continue through tonight. A gradual turn toward the
northeast and north is expected on Friday and Saturday.

or so, followed by weakening through the weekend.

center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 140 miles
(220 km).

item.title: Hurricane Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 19
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM PDT Thu Sep 24 2026 
716 
WTPZ41 KNHC 242034
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Odalys Discussion Number  19
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 PM PDT Thu Sep 24 2026
 
There are hints of a ragged eye feature in recent visible satellite 
images of Odalys. A 1735 UTC 89 GHz GMI image of the hurricane 
showed a mostly closed mid-level eyewall, although convection was a 
bit thin on the west side due to moderate westerly shear. The 
various UW-CIMSS objective satellite intensity estimates range from 
71-84 kt. The initial intensity is held at 80 kt, in best agreement 
with recent D-MINT and SATCON estimates.

Odalys is moving east-northeastward (060/7 kt) while being steered 
by a mid- to upper-level trough to its northwest. The models 
generally agree that the hurricane should gradually turn toward the 
northeast and north over the next couple of days. There was a 
westward shift in the guidance envelope through the first 2-3 days 
of the forecast, and the NHC prediction was adjusted accordingly. 
The long-range track forecast is challenging, with Odalys forecast 
to become increasingly shallow while weakening and also possibly 
being influenced by the outer circulation of Hurricane Polo. The 
model spread greatly increases at 72-120 h, but the general signal 
is for a slower forward speed and a southward component of motion at 
days 3-5. The NHC forecast was nudged west of the previous one at 
these times, falling in between the latest TVCN and HCCA aids.

In the near term, small intensity fluctuations are possible as the 
improved structure of Odalys could allow for a little strengthening 
despite moderate shear and the potential for intrusion of drier air 
from the west. The latest intensity guidance shows little change 
during this period, and the NHC forecast follows suit. After 36 h, 
a faster rate of weakening is forecast based on an expected 
increase in shear, as well as decreasing SSTs along the forecast 
track. These conditions will likely make it difficult for Odalys to 
sustain organized convection later this weekend, and the updated 
forecast shows Odalys as a post-tropical cyclone at 72 h based on 
the latest GFS and ECMWF simulated satellite imagery.
 
Moisture from both Odalys and Polo will be carried a long distance 
into the southwestern U.S. this weekend and early next week, and may 
indirectly contribute to a heavy rainfall and flash flood threat in 
the region. See products issued by the Weather Prediction Center for 
more information.

item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Thu Sep 24 2026 
000
WTPZ32 KNHC 242050
TCPEP2
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Advisory Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
300 PM CST Thu Sep 24 2026
 
...NOAA HURRICANE HUNTER AIRCRAFT REPORTS THAT POLO'S WINDS ARE
NEAR 150 MPH...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 PM CST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.1N 105.5W
ABOUT 155 MI...245 KM SSW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 490 MI...790 KM SE OF CABO SAN LUCAS MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...150 MPH...240 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 285 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...935 MB...27.61 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The Meteorological Service of Mexico has discontinued the Tropical
Storm Warning and Tropical Storm Watch for the southwestern coast
of Mexico.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests elsewhere along the coast of southwestern Mexico and Baja
California Sur should monitor the progress of this system.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 PM CST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Polo was located
near latitude 17.1 North, longitude 105.5 West. Polo is moving
toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h). A turn toward the
west is expected later today and Friday, followed by a west-
northwestward motion on Saturday. On the forecast track, the core
of Polo is expected to move away from the coast of southwestern
Mexico this afternoon and evening.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 150 mph (240 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Polo is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale.  Some strengthening is expected tonight. 
Gradual weakening is forecast to occur starting Friday night and 
Saturday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The minimum central pressure estimated from NOAA Hurricane Hunter
aircraft data is 935 mb (27.61 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Wind gusts to tropical-storm force are possible along
portions of the coast of southwestern Mexico this evening.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce additional rainfall totals of
2 to 4 inches, with isolated maximum totals up to 6 inches across
coastal portions of the Mexican states of Michoacan, Colima,
northern and southern Jalisco, and Nayarit. This rainfall may
produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas
of steep terrain. Additional rainfall of 1 to 2 inches is possible
in coastal portions of the Mexican states of central Jalisco and
Guerrero.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF: Swells generated by Polo will affect portions of the coast of
southwestern Mexico during the next couple of days. Swells will
spread northward along the coast of west-central Mexico and toward
Baja California Sur on Friday and into the weekend. These swells are
likely to cause life-threatening surf, rip currents, and coastal
flooding. Please consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 900 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Beven

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 300 PM CST Thu Sep 24 2026 
ZCZC MIATCDEP2 ALL
TTAA00 KNHC DDHHMM
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
300 PM CST Thu Sep 24 2026
 
A NOAA Hurricane Hunter aircraft has investigated Polo during the
past few hours, and its data indicates that the eyewall replacement
cycle mentioned in the previous advisory is almost complete. The 
first aircraft pass reported concentric eyewalls of 15 and 30 n mi 
diameters. Subsequent passes reported that the inner eyewall 
dissipated, while the remaining outer eyewall contracted to 25 n mi 
diameter. In addition, 700-mb flight level winds in the northeast 
eyewall increased by about 15 kt during the mission, with the 
maximum winds of 147 kt.  The central pressure also started to fall 
during the mission, and the estimated value from data on the last 
pass is near 935 mb. Based on these data, the initial intensity is 
set at 130 kt. It should be noted that the strengthening observed 
by the aircraft has not yet been fully reflected in satellite 
imagery.
 
Polo is now moving west-northwestward or 285/9 kt. There is little 
change to the track forecast reasoning from the previous advisory. 
A mid-level ridge building westward from northern Mexico should 
steer the hurricane generally westward for the next 24-36 h or so. 
After that, a mid-latitude trough moving eastward across the
northeastern Pacific should prevent the ridge from building farther
west, with Polo likely to recurve northward and northeastward
around the western end of the ridge. The track guidance is 
generally in good agreement with this scenario, although there 
remains some spread in the forward speed between the slower HAFS 
models and the faster GFS and HCCA models. The new track, which is 
an update of the previous forecast, takes the center away from the 
southwestern coast of Mexico this evening and then has it moving 
across Baja California into northwestern mainland Mexico in 96-120 
h.
 
The new intensity forecast now calls for Polo to strengthen for the
next 12 h or so after the end of the eyewall replacement, and Polo
is expected to regain Category 5 strength tonight or Friday
morning. After that, a slow weakening is expected through 96 h as
Polo encounters somewhat increased shear, with the caveat that
there could be some fluctuations due to additional eyewall
replacement cycles. Rapid weakening is expected when the cyclone
crosses Baja California and moves into mainland Mexico. The new
forecast again lies near the upper edge of the intensity guidance.

It should be noted that moisture from Hurricane Polo and Odalys 
will be carried a long distance into the southwestern United States 
this weekend and early next week, and may indirectly contribute to 
a heavy rainfall and flash flood threat in the region. See products 
issued by the Weather Prediction Center for more information.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo will impact coastal portions
of southwest Mexico today. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.

2. Wind gusts to tropical storm force may occur along portions of 
the southwestern coast of Mexico this evening.
 
3. Polo is forecast to approach the Baja California Peninsula early
next week as a hurricane. Interests there should closely monitor
the latest updates and ensure that they have their preparedness
plan in place.
